newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO INTRODUCE TOURIST SERVICE LICENCES.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO INTRODUCE TOURIST SERVICE LICENCES.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday approved a draft law which would oblige tourist agencies to secure a government licence for operations, a government official said.

Under the bill, agencies organising package tours and providing complex tourist services will have to seek a licence from a government's body called the Sports and Tourism Office (UKFiT), UKFiT's head Stefan Paszczyk told a news briefing.
The bill, which now goes to parliament for approval, does not require licences for running hotels, lending tourist equipment and providing other simple services.
Paszczyk said the bill was needed to protect customers of against the numerous dishonest and unreliable agencies which have sprouted in Poland over the past several years.
